key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar cell stacks and pinpoint the most influential design parameters for high-efficiency, lead-free architectures.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical screening strategy for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL choices in perovskite devices, reducing the need for exhaustive simulation or experimental trial-and-error.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen architectures.
Used SHAP to identify key descriptors and verify top-ranked designs with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking performance, and the top predicted devices were confirmed by SCAPS-1D, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE and FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.62% PCE.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the simulated training subset, so real-device validation is still needed to confirm transferability across fabrication conditions and material defects.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
